a.label: Area 51 (Homey Airport / Groom Lake operating location)

edges.label: Area 51 is the named facility on the Groom Lake shore
edges.note: The operating location is carried on charts as Homey Airport and sits on the southwest shore of the Groom Lake salt flat inside R-4808N.

edges.label: Edwards defines the acknowledged-testing boundary that Groom Lake was built to escape
edges.note: Groom Lake exists because the U-2 could not be tested at Edwards. The pair therefore mark the boundary between the acknowledged and unacknowledged US flight test enterprise.

edges.label: Knapp broadcast the Lazar interviews from KLAS-TV Las Vegas in 1989
edges.note: The May 1989 KLAS-TV interviews created the public reverse-engineering narrative attached to Area 51 and S-4.

edges.label: The Groom and Tonopah workforce commutes from Las Vegas
edges.note: The unmarked JANET fleet operates from a dedicated terminal at the Las Vegas airport. Reasoning: publicly observable daily operations; no primary personnel or contract record has been obtained.

b.label: Nellis Air Force Base and the Nevada Test and Training Range

edges.label: Groom Lake was administratively carried as part of the Nellis complex
edges.note: Until the 1995 presidential determination, the official position was that Groom Lake was simply another part of the Nellis Air Force Base complex.

b.label: STAR GATE and predecessor remote viewing programs, 1970-1995

edges.label: Both are demonstrations of decades-long concealment ending in bulk declassification
edges.note: Groom Lake ran 58 years to specific acknowledgement via FOIA; STAR GATE ran 25 years to bulk CREST publication in 2017. Reasoning: structural comparison of two documented concealment lifecycles.

edges.label: Programmes matured from Groom Lake to operational basing at Tonopah
edges.note: HAVE IDEA moved to Tonopah in May 1973; the 4450th Tactical Group moved from Groom Lake to Tonopah beginning 17 May 1982 to operate the F-117A.

a.label: Lockheed Martin Advanced Development Programs (Skunk Works)

edges.label: Skunk Works aircraft were tested at Groom Lake because they could not be tested at Edwards
edges.note: The CIA's own history records that U-2 flight test and pilot training could not be conducted at Edwards or Palmdale given the secrecy of the project. The U-2, A-12, HAVE BLUE and F-117 all flew first at Groom.
